Group regulation actions in collaborative learning

Source: R/data.R
group_regulation_long.Rd

group_regulation_long is a coded dataset of students' regulation actions during collaborative learning: 27,533 timestamped actions by 2,000 students working in 200 groups across three courses. It is in long format, one row per action.

Usage

group_regulation_long

Format

A data frame with 27,533 rows and 6 columns:

Actor

Integer student identifier, 1 to 2,000.

Achiever

Character achievement level, "High" or "Low".

Group

Numeric collaboration group identifier, 1 to 200; each student belongs to one group.

Course

Character course identifier, "A", "B" or "C".

Time

POSIXct timestamp of the action.

Action

Character regulation action, one of adapt, cohesion, consensus, coregulate, discuss, emotion, monitor, plan and synthesis.

Source

Synthetically generated from the group_regulation dataset in the tna package.

See also

learning_activities, srl_strategies

Examples

net <- build_network(group_regulation_long,
                     method = "relative",
                     actor = "Actor", action = "Action", time = "Time")
net
#> Transition Network (relative probabilities) [directed]
#>   Weights: [0.001, 0.498]  |  mean: 0.115
#> 
#>   Strongest edges (10 of 78):
#>    from      to        weight
#>    cohesion  consensus 0.498 
#>    adapt     consensus 0.477 
#>    synthesis consensus 0.466 
#>    consensus plan      0.396 
#>    monitor   discuss   0.375 
#>    plan      plan      0.374 
#>    emotion   cohesion  0.325 
#>    discuss   consensus 0.321 
#>    emotion   consensus 0.320 
#>    plan      consensus 0.290  
#> 
#>   extract_edges(include_self = TRUE) lists every edge; extract_transition_matrix() gives the weight matrix;
#>   extract_initial_probs() the initial probabilities.
